 O R D E R
The dispute inter se the parties, after the transfer of the case pending before the trial Court was directed, was referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre at the joint request of the parties.
In pursuance to the same, in a mediation settlement, apparently the parties have agreed to a joint compromise.
It is set out in the settlement Reason: agreement that the marriage between the parties was solemnized as per Hindu rites on 02.12.2015 and the parties resided together till 20.07.2016.
They separated due to irretrievable disputes and differences and there are no issues out of the wedlock.

In terms of the single settlement agreement, the parties have agreed to a mutual consent divorce under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage Jaideep Singh Sond vs Abanti Mazumder on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148393305/
1 and the petitioner has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.24 lakh to the respondent by an electronic transfer in full and final settlement of all her claims towards permanent alimony or otherwise.

sentences.text: The parties seek a decree of divorce invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and also seek quashing/withdrawal of the cases filed inter se the parties details of which have been submitted in para 4 of the terms of settlement.

On having perused the application, we find the settlement duly signed by the parties, their counsels and learned Mediator and we are inclined to invoke our jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to grant a decree of divorce by mutual consent in terms of the settlement agreement which shall form part of the order.
The amount of permanent alimony agreed upon is stated to have already been transferred.

The decree of divorce be accordingly drawn up and the proceedings in respect of the cases enumerated in para 4 would stand withdrawn/quashed, the details of which are as under:
4(1) Baguihati PS case No.1129 of 2018 under Ss.406,498A, 307, 506, 406 and IPC (Converted to GR 4057/2016 pending before LD.2nd JM, District Court, Barasat,
North 24, Parganas, West Bengal stands quashed.
( II )
M.C. No.3659 of 2018 under Section 13(1) (a) pending before Ld. Principal Judge, Family Court, Bangalore
stands withdrawn.
It may be noted that two other case have already been dismissed as enumerated in para 4 (III).
The Miscellaneous Application stands disposed of.

We appreciate the constructive approach adopted by the parties and the counsel to bring this dispute to an end.
...J. [SANJAY KISHAN KAUL] ...J.
